<h2>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">2026 DACoP meeting dates</span>




</h2>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<ul>
<li>26 February</li>
<li>26 March</li>
<li>30 April</li>
<li>28 May</li>
<li>25 June</li>
<li>30 July</li>
<li>27 August</li>
<li>24 September</li>
<li>29 October</li>
<li>26 November</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>

<h2>Future presentations</h2>
<h3>30 July: UI design systems for digital delivery</h3>
<p>Peter Koenders from Ministry of Social Development (MSD) will explore how a UI design system provides a shared foundation for consistent, accessible digital delivery. He'll discuss what a design system is (and is not), how it supports teams working at scale, accessibility by design, measurable outcomes, and the role of governance, contribution, and continuous improvement.</p>
<h3>27 August: Using AI to improve accessibility</h3>
<p>Accessible communications enable disabled people to have information at the same time as everyone else. Yet for many disabled people, everyday information is still hard to access.</p>
<p>Whaikaha-Ministry of Disabled People are addressing this by strengthening how all-of-government information is provided in alternate formats including audio, Braille, Easy Read, large print and NZSL.</p>
<p>Jasmine Lindsay, Manager of Operations and Delivery at Whaikaha will discuss how AI is being piloted to improve document accessibility and support kaimahi to create clearer, plain-language information. She will share the Whaikaha AI journey so far, take a closer look at the document accessibility pilot, and reflect on what's shown promise, what's been challenging, and what others might take forward in their own work.</p>
<h3>24 September: Lightning talks</h3>
<p>Lightning talks are short, 5-10 minute talks on a particular topic, in this case accessibility. We have had a few people express their interest in sharing a range of exciting topics. But there is still room for more people.</p>
<p>If you have something small that you'd like to share with the community, maybe doing a lightning talk is the perfect format for you. If you're keen, email&nbsp;<a rel="noopener noreferrer" href="mailto:web.standards@gdda.govt.nz" target="_blank">web.standards@gdda.govt.nz</a> to let us know.</p>


<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h2">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Previous presentations" data-ga-label="/home">
<h2>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Previous presentations</span>




</h2>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<h3>25 June 2026</h3>
<h4>What resonates when introducing accessibility? Reflections from 2 design lecturers</h4>
<p>Drs Catherine Cauldwell and Gillian McCarthy discussed how arguments for greater accessibility awareness resonate with students, and where the students see opportunities to make improvements in their own workplaces.</p>
<h3>28 May 2026</h3>
<p>Dr Claire Bretherton from Whaikaha – Ministry of Disabled People shared their recent experience accessible surveys for consulting with disabled people.</p>
<h3>30 April 2026</h3>
<p>Katherine Barcham from the Government Digital Delivery Agency (GDDA) talked about:</p>
<ul>
<li>how hidden disabilities can affect how our audience understands or interacts with our content</li>
<li>what you can do to make your writing stand up to the test.</li>
</ul>
<h3>26 March 2026</h3>
<h4>Digital accessibility coaching: a practical experience</h4>
<p>Chandra Harrison from Access Advisors talked about her experience mentoring a group of 4 Victoria University students participating in the Masters UX Design Capstone project.</p>
<p>The goal was to give them hands-on experience with digital accessibility — evaluating real not-for-profit websites, identifying issues, and designing improvements using best practice guidelines.</p>
<h3>26 February 2026</h3>
<h4>Free accessibility tools and how to use them</h4>
<p>Maia Miller from Aleph Accessibility explored a range of free tools that fit into each part of the development lifecycle. These can help you check, improve and maintain accessibility in your digital products.</p>
<h3>2025 Presentations</h3>
<ul>
<li>November - Getting accessibility ready for a design system (Intopia)</li>
<li>October – Whaikaha Ministry of Disabled People: Accessibility Charter, alternate formats, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) strategy</li>
<li>September – Gaining senior stakeholder engagement (Catalyst)</li>
<li>August – Research insights from the Digital Accessibility Standard (Katherine Barcham, Web Standards team)</li>
<li>July – Basic accessibility testing (Ministry of Social Development (MSD))</li>
<li>June – Accessibility in large-scale web development (Department of Conservation)</li>
<li>May – Accessible documents and training for screen reader users (Wellington City Council and MSD)</li>
<li>April – EN 301 549 demystified (Jason Kiss, Web Standards team)</li>
<li>March – Structured accessibility audits (MSD)</li>
<li>February – DACoP welcome and updates (Web Standards team)</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>

<h2>What DACoP is about</h2>
<p>DACoP brings together people from the public and private sectors who care about digital accessibility. Each month there are presentations and discussions that explore practical solutions, share lessons learned, and highlight different approaches to accessibility.</p>
<p>It’s a place to:</p>
<ul>
<li>hear from others working in the field</li>
<li>ask questions — technical, theoretical, or practical</li>
<li>discover best practices and new resources</li>
<li>connect with a supportive network of peers.</li>
</ul>
<p>Whether you're just starting out or have years of experience, DACoP is here to support your journey.</p>
<h2>Join DACoP</h2>
<p>To join the Digital Accessibility Community of Practice, email web.standards@gdda.govt.nz. You will get a link to the monthly Teams meetings and you will be added to the mailing list.</p>
<h2>Who can join</h2>
<p>DACoP is open to anyone with an interest in digital accessibility. You do not need to work for government and you do not need to be an expert — just be curious and keen to learn. The community includes designers, developers, policy advisors, testers, content creators and more.</p>
<h2>Who runs DACoP</h2>
<p>DACoP is hosted by the Web Standards team at the Government Digital Delivery Agency (GDDA). The team supports the work of the Government Chief Digital Officer (GCDO) by maintaining the NZ Government Web Standards and helping government agencies to meet them.</p>
<h2>DACoP mailing list</h2>
<p>DACoP members will receive 1 email a month including things like:</p>
<ul>
<li>topics of interest from the community</li>
<li>upcoming presentations</li>
<li>recent accessibility guidance and resources</li>
<li>news or invitations to accessibility-related events</li>
<li>updates from the Web Standards team.</li>
</ul>
<p>To opt out at any time, email <a href="mailto:web.standards@gdda.govt.nz">web.standards@gdda.govt.nz</a>. You’re still welcome to attend sessions even if you’re not on the mailing list.</p>
<h2>Monthly sessions</h2>
<p>DACoP meets online using Microsoft Teams on the last Thursday of each month, from 10am to 12pm. Attendance is free and you can come and go as you like, depending on your schedule.</p>
<p>To get the Teams link, email <a href="mailto:web.standards@gdda.govt.nz">web.standards@gdda.govt.nz</a>.</p>
<h3>Session format</h3>
<p>Each session typically includes 1 or 2 presentations, followed by open discussion. The format is informal and supportive — perfect for asking questions and sharing ideas.</p>
<h3>Sessions are not recorded</h3>
<p>To foster open conversation, sessions are not recorded. We only record the organisations represented and the topics discussed.</p>
